final_rationale: The verdict remains noncompliant because no genuinely new admissible evidence was added after the Actor response. The response materially narrows the claim and correctly concedes the core defect, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence. The admissible evidence still shows an exposed below-target launch segment, no exclusion of that segment from rollout, and no approved risk acceptance or documented disclosure satisfying the policy condition. A caveated monitored-launch rationale may describe the business posture, but it does not convert the unresolved policy predicate into compliance. The distinction is that caveats can qualify a supportable launch rationale, but they cannot replace a required disclosure or approved acceptance when the policy makes that a condition of compliance.
remaining_concerns: The small-business onboarding segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort despite being below target on long-context onboarding support.
The policy requires disclosure before launch unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance when the affected segment remains exposed.
The available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete: the approver line is blank and it does not address the small-business onboarding exposure.
There is no admissible evidence of the required disclosure, no approved risk acceptance, and no rollout exclusion for the affected segment.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one incidents, 6% rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the policy predicate on this record.
